consensus_summary: Righteousness primarily means right standing before God and conformity to His character/standard, most prominently as Christ's imputed righteousness received by faith (with right conduct as fruit, evidence, or related sense); mechanisms remain debated across imputed, infused, covenantal, and ethical readings.
book_summary: Right-living. God is Right-Living by definition; for those under His authority, righteousness is His commandments lived out. Opposite: Sin.
consensus_core_identification: right standing before God (esp. imputed/forensic status) plus conformity to His standard
boundary_disagreement: Consensus treats forensic/imputed standing as central cases of the term itself (living as subsequent fruit); book excludes standing-as-definition, reclassifying it as common teaching only, and centers solely on obedient conduct.
material_contradiction: Book equates the term with lived commandments/conduct (opposite sin), requiring rejection of the consensus primary identification of the term with right standing/imputed status.
rationale: Minimum cores differ in referent: consensus centers status/standing before God (living related or derivative); book replaces that with right-living as the definition itself, explicitly noting and setting aside the common imputed-standing view. Causal fruit relation does not preserve identity of referent. Extension therefore tracks a different primary object even where some conduct cases overlap.
strongest_objection: Printed references still include classic imputation texts (Rom 4:4-8; Phil 3:9), which the consensus reads as defining the term forensically rather than as lived commandments.
